name: PALESTINE
lead: Palestine sits where three continents meet. Old olive trees shade its valleys. Palestinians are famous for warm welcomes and poems about home. Ramallah has busy cafés. Jerusalem draws pilgrims from three world religions.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The West Bank has hills of olive and almond trees. The Jordan Valley drops to the Dead Sea. It lies 430 m below sea level, the lowest land on Earth.
The Gaza Strip is a narrow ribbon on the Mediterranean coast. It is just 41 km long and 10 km wide. Over two million people live there.
animals: Huge flocks of storks, pelicans, and eagles fly over Palestine each spring and autumn. The tiny Palestine sunbird, with a shiny green throat, is the national bird.
Mountain gazelles dart across the hillsides. Striped hyenas and red foxes hide in the rocks. So do rock hyraxes, small cousins of elephants.
culture: Maqluba is upside-down rice and vegetables. Musakhan is chicken on flatbread with onions and sumac. Knafeh is hot cheese pastry in syrup. Olive oil goes on almost everything.
Tatreez is red embroidery that tells stories of village and family. Dabke is a stomping line dance at weddings. The oud, a pear-shaped lute, fills evenings with music.
history: People farmed these hills since 9000 BCE. Canaanites, Egyptians, Greeks, Romans, and Crusaders all left marks. The name Palestine echoes the ancient Philistines of the coast.

After Ottoman rule, Britain controlled the region from 1917. Israel was declared in 1948, and around 700,000 Palestinians fled. They call this the Nakba, meaning 'catastrophe'. Palestinians have sought an independent state ever since.
wows: People have lived in Jericho, maybe Earth's oldest city, for 11,000 years.
The Dead Sea is nearly 10 times saltier than the ocean.
An olive tree near Bethlehem may be up to 5,000 years old.
The tiny Palestine sunbird hovers like a helicopter.
Each village has its own tatreez patterns, like a postcode.
Nablus holds a festival for knafeh, the hot cheese pastry.
The name Gaza appears in Egyptian records 3,500 years old.

myths.myth: Arabic is written left to right
myths.fact: Arabic runs right to left. Its books open at what English readers call the back.

myths.myth: The Dead Sea is actually a sea
myths.fact: It is a salt lake with no way out to the ocean.
